def sum_Of_Subarray_Prod(arr):
    total_sum = 0
    
    # Iterate through every possible starting index i
    for i in range(len(arr)):
        current_product = 1
        
        # Extend the sublist from start index i to end index j
        for j in range(i, len(arr)):
            # Multiply by the next element (inclusive of arr[j])
            current_product *= arr[j]
            
            # Add this subarray's product to the total sum
            total_sum += current_product
            
    return total_sum

# Test cases based on your requirement and additional examples
if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert sum_Of_Subarray_Prod([1, 2, 3]) == 20
    
    # Additional test case: [4] -> only one subarray [4], product = 4
    assert sum_Of_Subarray_Prod([4]) == 4
    
    # Test case with negative numbers to ensure correctness logic holds
    # Subarrays of [-1, -2]: 
    # [-1]=(-1), [-2]=(-2), [-1,-2]=(2) -> Sum = -3 + (-2) + 2 = -3? Wait.
    # Let's re-calculate manually for [-1, -2]:
    # [ -1 ]: prod = -1
    # [ -2 ]: prod = -2
    # [ -1, -2 ]: prod = (-1)*(-2) = 2
    # Sum = -1 + -2 + 2 = -1.
    
    assert sum_Of_Subarray_Prod([-1, -2]) == -1
    
    print("All assertions passed.")
